name: watch_login
prose: tcsh's check of the utmp file for logins and logouts of users named in the "watch" variable (tc.who.c:195-453, slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It disables interrupts with a cleanup registered (221-222) and every early return runs cleanup_until(&pintr_disabled). It returns at once if "watch" is unset and force is 0, or if less than the interval has passed since the last check (224-242). It then stats the utmp file; a failed stat prints a message (unless force) and returns, an unchanged modification time (stlast) returns, otherwise stlast is advanced to the new time before the file is read (248-260). Without getutent support, if the open fails it prints a message (unless force) and returns after stlast has already been advanced, so no scan happens (264-271). Otherwise it marks every entry in the status list OFFLINE|CLEARED and reads the utmp records, skipping non-user records, updating the matching tty entry (offline, online-announced, or changed) or inserting a new one in sorted order (279-388). If force is set or no watch list exists it returns here (396-399); otherwise for each user/terminal pair of the watch list it announces, unless firsttime, the entries that went offline, came online or changed, and updates their names and ANNOUNCE flags (405-451), then it releases the cleanup and returns (452).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits the early return when utmp open fails; stlast already advanced and no scan occurs - right (260 then 264-271, in the non-getutent build). Read in full (many #ifdef variants are summarised together); print_who, trim, number and xopen not read.

name: tw_result
prose: Maps a completion action string act (from a tcsh "complete" definition) to a TW_* look-up code and an optional pattern; defined at tw.comp.c:266-396 (slice cut the head). It frees the static result buffer res left by an earlier call (272-273). It switches on act[0] with the QUOTE bit masked off: letters select a single look-up kind, for example 'X' completion, 'S' signal, 'a' alias, 'b' binding, 'c' command, 'C' path-and-command, 'd' directory, 'D' path-and-directory, 'e' environment variable, 'f' file, 'F' (and 'p' when COMPAT is defined) path-and-file, 'g' group, 'j' job, 'l' limit, 'n' none, 's' shell variable, 't' text, 'T' path-and-text, 'v' variable, 'u' user, 'x' explain (276-341). '$' stores a copy of the rest of act in *pat and res, strips it and returns TW_VARLIST (343-346); '(' stores the text up to a ')' in *pat and returns TW_WORDLIST (348-353); '`' copies act, makes sure descriptors 0 to 2 are set up if needed, runs globone on the command text and returns TW_WORDLIST with the result in *pat, or TW_ZERO if it gives NULL (355-376). Any other first character raises the stderror ERR_COMPCOM and returns TW_ZERO (378-380). For the letter cases it then looks at act[1] with the QUOTE bit masked off: '\0' (including a QUOTE-masked end) returns the look-up code, ':' stores a stripped copy of the text after it in *pat and returns the code, and any other character gives the ERR_COMPCOM error and TW_ZERO (383-394).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits QUOTE-masked act[0]/act[1]; act[1]==QUOTE returns looking, not stderror - right (275 and 383 mask with ~QUOTE, so act[1]==QUOTE hits case '\0' at 384-385). Slice cut the head; function read in full; globone, stderror and Strsave not read.

name: t_search
prose: Searches for completions of the word in tcsh's tab completion; defined at tw.parse.c:1510-1827 (slice cut the head) and returns an item count (or -1, 0 or 2 in special cases) in res. It clears the previous items, splits word into directory and name parts (1528-1534) and decides the kind of look-up: a word starting with '~' and containing no '/' becomes TW_LOGNAME, and a name with an unbraced '$' and no '/' becomes TW_VARIABLE (1542-1556). With TW_PATH set it builds the directory from pat and the typed directory (1561-1567). It then handles some kinds before collecting: TW_NONE returns -1 (1572-1574), TW_EXPLAIN prints the explanation for LIST and returns 2 (1601-1609), and other kinds set flags (1571-1618). It opens or expands the directory as the kind requires; failures return -1 (expand_dir results returned as they are, a failed opendir prints an error and returns -1, unknown kind prints an internal error and returns -1, 1624-1771). For the SPELL command on a name that is already a valid user it returns 0 (1748-1753). It then calls tw_collect, and if that returns -1 the function returns -1 (1775-1778); otherwise it acts on command: the recognize commands fix the word and add a suffix when exactly one item matched, LIST lists the items, SPELL fixes the word, and any other command value prints "Bad tw_command" and sets numitems to 0, so the function returns 0 rather than -1 in that case (1780-1821). The result is numitems (1822-1823) and the cleanup happens at err_dir (1824-1826).
note: [R:right] reviewer: a bad command sets numitems=0 and returns 0, not -1 - right (1818-1823). Slice cut the head; function read in full; tw_collect, expand_dir, tw_fixword and tw_list_items not read.

name: cfb64_is
prose: Telnet encryption suboption handler for the DES CFB64 mode (enc_des.c:233-236): it returns fb64_is(data, cnt, &fb[CFB]), so everything it does and returns is what fb64_is does for the CFB entry of the fb[] table.
note: [R:n/a] one-line wrapper at enc_des.c:233-236 (slice cut the head), read in full; the behaviour is that of fb64_is, whose description is given in its own record.

name: ofb64_is
prose: Telnet encryption suboption handler for the DES OFB64 mode (enc_des.c:239-242): it returns fb64_is(data, cnt, &fb[OFB]), so everything it does and returns is what fb64_is does for the OFB entry of the fb[] table.
note: [R:n/a] one-line wrapper at enc_des.c:239-242, read in full.

name: fb64_is
prose: Handles an incoming encryption suboption for the DES feedback modes (enc_des.c:245-307). It takes the current decrypt state fbp->state[DIR_DECRYPT-1] into a local variable. If cnt is below 1 it goes to the failure label with the state unchanged (250-251). If the first byte is FB64_IV and the remaining length is not sizeof(Block) it sets the local state to FAILED and goes to failure (255-260). If the length matches, it installs the IV into the decrypt stream with fb64_stream_iv, builds an ENCRYPT_REPLY with the FB64_IV_OK suboption, sends it with net_write (after printsub) and sets both the stored state and the local state to IN_PROGRESS (268-280). Any other first byte prints a debug message when encrypt_debug_mode is set and falls into the failure code (282-289). The failure code builds an ENCRYPT_REPLY with the FB64_IV_BAD suboption and writes it to the network (295-302). All paths end with fbp->state[DIR_DECRYPT-1] = state and return that value (306), so a failure with a bad size stores FAILED, and the other failures store the unchanged previous state.
note: [R:mixed] reviewers: (1) prose says the result is -1/0/1 but the code returns the state value - right (306); (2) prose omits a NO_RECV_IV guard so the IV is installed only when the bit is set - wrong: no such guard exists in this function (253-280); (3) a well-formed IV does not set the state to 7 - right, the code stores IN_PROGRESS (279; the numeric value of IN_PROGRESS not read). Read in full; fb64_stream_iv, net_write and printsub not read.

name: encrypt_keyid
prose: Processes a key identifier received for an encryption direction (encrypt.c:711-752); it returns nothing. It clamps len to MAXKEYLEN (717-718) and gets the current encryption type through kp->getcrypt. When no type is available: len==0 returns at once, otherwise kp->keylen is set to 0 (720-723). When the new length is 0 (an empty option, meaning failure): it returns at once if the stored keylen is already 0, otherwise clears keylen and, if the type has a keyid callback, calls it (724-733). When the length or the contents differ from the stored key id it stores the new id and calls the keyid callback if there is one (734-742). In those three non-returning cases it ends by sending the key id back with encrypt_send_keyid (751). When the id is unchanged it returns without sending anything: it calls the keyid callback if there is one and keeps ret = 0 when there is none, and if ret is 0, the direction is DIR_ENCRYPT and autoencrypt is set it starts output with encrypt_start_output (743-748).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the unchanged branch also starts output when no keyid callback exists (ret defaults 0) - right (715 initialises ret to 0 and 744-747 only sets it when ep->keyid is non-NULL). Slice cut the head; function at encrypt.c:711-752 read in full; callbacks not read.

name: kerberos5_reply
prose: Handles a Kerberos V5 telnet authentication reply (kerberos5.c:568-654, slice cut the head); it returns nothing and keeps a static mutual_complete flag. It returns at once if cnt is below 1 (572-573) and switches on the first byte. KRB_REJECT prints the refusal (with the reason text if any), calls auth_send_retry and returns (575-582). KRB_ACCEPT: if mutual authentication was required and mutual_complete is not set it prints a message, calls auth_send_retry and returns (588-593); otherwise it prints the acceptance, fetches the local subkey (or the key if that fails), and if that fetch fails it prints the error, calls auth_send_retry and returns (599-610); on success it passes the 8-byte key to encrypt_session_key, frees the key block, calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_USER), and forwards credentials with kerberos5_forward when OPTS_FORWARD_CREDS is set, then leaves the switch (612-620). KRB_RESPONSE with mutual authentication runs krb5_rd_rep: on failure it prints the error, calls auth_send_retry and returns, on success it sets mutual_complete to 1; both then return (622-641). KRB_FORWARD_ACCEPT and KRB_FORWARD_REJECT print a message and return (642-648); an unknown byte prints a debug message when auth_debug_mode is set and returns (649-652).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits the KRB_ACCEPT key-fetch failure path (print error, auth_send_retry) - right (606-609). Read in full; the Kerberos library calls and auth_send_retry not read.

name: sra_is
prose: Handles an incoming SRA telnet authentication suboption on the server side (sra.c:151-238). If cnt is below 1 it goes to the bad label (156-157). SRA_KEY: if fewer than HEXKEYBYTES bytes follow it sends SRA_REJECT, calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_USER) and returns (161-168); otherwise it sends the server public key, returns if there is not enough room to send it, and stores the client key in pkb and calls common_key before returning (171-179). SRA_USER: more than 512 bytes breaks out to the bad code (183-184); otherwise it decodes the user name with pk_decode, calls auth_encrypt_user(user), sends SRA_CONTINUE and returns (185-191). SRA_PASS: more than 512 bytes breaks to the bad code (194-195); otherwise it decodes the password and calls check_user; if valid it sends SRA_ACCEPT, installs the session key, sets sra_valid to 1 and calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_VALID); if not valid it sends SRA_CONTINUE (202-228); both return. Any other option prints a debug message when auth_debug_mode is set and falls to the bad code (230-233). The bad code sends SRA_REJECT, sets sra_valid to 0 and calls auth_finished(ap, AUTH_REJECT) (234-237).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits the auth_encrypt_user(user) side effect on the SRA_USER path - right (188). Slice cut the head; function read in full; pk_decode, common_key, check_user and Data not read.

name: sourceroute
prose: Builds an IP or IPv6 source-route option from the text arg (a list such as @host1,host2 or !@host...), storing it in *cpp and its length in *lenp; defined at commands.c:2852-3017 (slice cut the head). It returns -1 if cpp or lenp is NULL (2869-2870), and when *cpp is already a buffer it returns -1 if the buffer is smaller than the minimum for the address family, but this test reads res->ai_family before res has been assigned in this function (2871-2885). It uses the caller's buffer or its own static 1024-byte buffer (2890-2896). For IPv6 it calls inet6_rth_init and returns -1 on failure or if arg does not start with '@' (2901-2908); for IPv4 it writes the LSRR or SSRR option header after a '!' or default, returning -1 if arg does not start with '@' (2917-2929). It then loops over the comma- or '@'-separated host names, resolving each with getaddrinfo (first as numeric, then as a name if EAI_NONAME): on a resolution error it prints the error, sets *cpp to the text of that host and returns 0, which does not involve any addrinfo result (2964-2976). Each address is added with inet6_rth_add (returning 0 if that fails) or copied into the IPv4 option (2977-2988). After each address except the last it returns -1 if fewer than 4 bytes of room remain in the IPv4 buffer pointer (2996-2997, so the IPv6 path has no such room check and this return does not free the addrinfo result), otherwise it frees the result and continues (2998). At the end the IPv6 case sets the header length and *lenp, the IPv4 case stores the option length and returns -1 after setting *cpp and *lenp to 0 if the route has no address (3001-3011), pads with a NOP and sets *lenp (3012-3013). It frees the last result and returns 1 (3015-3016).
note: [R:right] reviewer: getaddrinfo failure does not leak addrinfo; the IPv6 path lacks a buffer-room check - right (2969-2976 returns with res unset; 2996 compares the IPv4 pointer lsrp, which is not advanced for IPv6, 2980-2981). Slice cut the head; function read in full; getaddrinfo helpers and the inet6_rth_* functions not read.

name: main
prose: Entry point of the BSD telnet client (telnet/main.c:113-382, slice cut the head). It turns off stdio buffering, calls tninit and TerminalSaveState, derives prompt from argv[0], sets rlogin to '~' when the program name starts with "rlog" (else _POSIX_VDISABLE), sets autologin to 1 with AUTHENTICATION or -1 without it, and turns on automatic encryption when ENCRYPTION is compiled in (123-146). It then parses the options with getopt: 4, 6, 8, B, E, K, L, N, Q, S, X, a, c, d, e, f, F, k, l, n, r, s, u, x, y and, when IPSEC is compiled in, P (153-344). In the -P handler any argument whose first two characters are "in" is stored as the input policy and, failing that, any argument whose first three characters are "out" as the output policy; other arguments call usage() (330-337), so the test is a prefix test and not an exact match. Unknown options and '?' call usage() (339-341). If autologin is still -1 it is set from rlogin (345-346). With remaining arguments, more than two calls usage(); otherwise it builds an argument list (adding -l user and the source address when given) and runs tn(): the function returns 0 if tn returns 1 and 1 otherwise, after a setjmp whose longjmp calls Exit(0) (351-375). With no arguments it sets a setjmp point and loops forever calling command(1, 0, 0) (377-380); the return 0 at 381 is not reached from the loop.
note: [R:right] reviewer: -P accepts any optarg beginning with "in"/"out", not only exact "in"/"out" - right (331-334 use strncmp with length 2 and 3). Slice cut the head; function read in full except the bodies of the per-option warning messages; tn, command, usage and the option helpers not read.

name: dooption
prose: Handles a received TELNET DO option request (telnet.c:419-525; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It first adjusts the will_wont_resp counter for the option, decrementing it once and, if it is still positive and the option state is WILL, once more (423-427). If the counter is then 0 and we do not currently want the option, it decides whether to accept it. TELOPT_TM: it sends WILL (without marking a pending reply), sets the want and state to WONT, and returns (434-442). Binary, NAWS, terminal speed, flow control, terminal type, SGA and (with ENCRYPTION) encrypt are accepted. NEW-ENVIRON, when OLD_ENVIRON is compiled in, first sends WONT for OLD_ENVIRON if that was in state WILL, then records telopt_environ and is accepted; OLD-ENVIRON itself is not accepted (it only breaks, so a WONT is sent) if NEW-ENVIRON is in state WILL, otherwise it is recorded and accepted (456-468). Authentication is accepted when autologin is set, and XDISPLOC when the DISPLAY environment variable is set (470-480). LINEMODE sets the want and state to WILL, sends WILL, initialises the SLC table and returns (with KLUDGELINEMODE it also clears kludgelinemode and sends DO SGA first, 482-491). Other options are not accepted. For an accepted option it sets the want state to WILL, sends WILL and calls setconnmode(0); for an unaccepted one it increments will_wont_resp[option] and sends WONT (498-505). If instead we already wanted the option, only LINEMODE is handled: with KLUDGELINEMODE it clears kludgelinemode and sends DO SGA, then sets the state to WILL, initialises the SLC table, sends DO SGA again (without the pending flag) and returns (511-520). Paths that did not return earlier end with set_my_state_will(option) (524).
note: [R:right] reviewers: (1) the OLD_ENVIRON conflict sends WONT, not WILL - right (459 sends WONT for OLD_ENVIRON and 461-463 break without accepting); (2) the LINEMODE else-branch also clears kludgelinemode and sends the initial DO SGA - right (513-520). Function read in full; the telnet send_*/set_* macros and slc_init not read.

name: complete
prose: tnftp command-line completion callback for libedit (complete.c:360-437; slice cut the head). It returns CC_ERROR if the edit line is as long as the global line buffer (372-373). Otherwise it copies the line into the global buffer, records the cursor position, saves the previous cursor argument number and offset in the static lastc_argc and lastc_argo, and splits the line with makeargv (370-378). It returns CC_ERROR if the offset of the cursor in its word is not smaller than the static word buffer (380-381). It sets dolist to 1 when the cursor is in the same word and offset as the previous call and the saved word still matches the text typed (so the next call lists the choices), else it copies the current word into the static buffer, and terminates the word at the cursor offset (383-391). If the cursor is in the first word (cursor_argc == 0) it returns complete_command(word, dolist) (393-394). Otherwise it looks up the command in margv[0]; an unknown or ambiguous command returns CC_ERROR (396-398), so the unknown-command error applies only when the cursor is beyond the first word. It then takes the command's completion string c_complete; if the cursor word number is beyond its length and its last letter is upper case, the number is clamped to the length, and if it is still beyond the length it returns CC_ERROR (399-407). Finally it dispatches on the letter for the cursor word: 'c' or 'C' command completion, 'l' or 'L' local file completion, 'n' or 'N' CC_ERROR, 'o' or 'O' option completion, 'r' or 'R' remote completion, which prints "Must be logged in to complete." and returns CC_REDISPLAY when not connected, and any other letter calls errx(1, ...) (409-434).
note: [R:right] reviewer: an unknown first word returns CC_ERROR only when cursor_argc>0; cursor_argc==0 calls complete_command - right (393-398). Slice cut the head; function read in full; makeargv, getcmd and the complete_* helpers not read.

name: pswitch
prose: Swaps the active connection state with the saved "proxy" connection state in tnftp (ftp.c:1737-1821; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It clears abrtflag and installs psabort as the SIGINT handler, saving the old handler (1762-1763). With flag nonzero it returns at once if proxy is already set; with flag zero it returns at once if proxy is not set; in both early-return cases the SIGINT handler is left as psabort (the restore at 1816 is not reached, 1764-1772). Otherwise it picks the source (ip) and destination (op) blocks from two static structures, toggles proxy, and exchanges the connection fields: connected, host name, control addresses, the in and out streams, type, current type, cpend, sunique, runique, mcase, ntflag with ntin and ntout, mapflag with mapin and mapout (1777-1815). It then restores the old SIGINT handler and, if abrtflag was set meanwhile, clears it and calls the old handler directly with SIGINT (1816-1820).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the early return leaves the SIGINT handler set to psabort, not unchanged - right (1763 installs psabort before the early returns at 1766 and 1772, and xsignal(SIGINT, oldintr) at 1816 is skipped). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: sendrequest
prose: Sends a local file or command output to the server with the given FTP command (tnftp ftp.c:659-886; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and reports failure through the global code (-1) and the cleanup it runs. If proxy is set it calls proxtrans and returns (688-691). It changes the transfer type if needed, installs a sigsetjmp point for aborts (on an abort during setup it drains pending replies, sets code to -1 and goes to cleanupsend, 698-703) and signal handlers. The source is stdin when local is "-", a popen of the text after '|' (failure sets code -1 and goes to cleanupsend), or a file opened with fopen, in which case only a failed open, or a file that is not a regular file according to fstat, sets code to -1 and goes to cleanupsend (706-733); stdin and piped input are therefore not required to be regular files. It then calls initconn (failure sets code -1 and goes to cleanupsend), seeks to restart_point for STOR or APPE when set (a failed seek or REST goes to cleanupsend), sends the command and opens the data connection, going to abort if dataconn fails (734-773). It copies the data with copy_bytes for image or local types or with a CRLF-translating loop for ASCII, ignoring SIGPIPE, then closes the input and data streams, reads the final reply and prints transfer statistics when bytes is positive (786-848). The abort label restores SIGINT and, when no reply is pending, sets code to -1 and goes to cleanupsend; otherwise it closes the data descriptor and stream, reads the reply, sets code to -1 and prints the statistics (850-868). cleanupsend restores the signal handlers, closes the data descriptor, input and data streams, and resets restart_point and bytes to 0 (870-885).
note: [R:right] reviewer: non-regular input (stdin/pipe) is supported and does not set code to -1 - right (the regular-file test at 727 is only in the last branch, for a named file). Slice cut the head; function read in full except messages; copy_bytes, initconn, dataconn and getreply not read.

name: slurpstring
prose: Extracts the next argument from the global command string stringbase into the argument area at argbase (tnftp main.c:832-959; slice cut the head). If the next character is '!' or '$' and slrflag is 0, it increments slrflag, advances stringbase by one character (INC_CHKCURSOR, not read) and returns a static one-character string "!" or "$"; if slrflag is 1 it increments slrflag and records altarg (841-855). It then skips leading blanks and tabs, increments slrflag on the first token, and records altarg for the second token (857-881). It copies characters into the argument area until a blank, tab or NUL, handling backslash (copies the next character literally) and double-quote (copies characters up to the closing quote) (883-937); a NUL inside a quote or after a backslash ends the token. At the end it terminates the argument with a NUL if any character was copied (got_one), advances argbase past it, stores the scan position in stringbase and returns the argument pointer (939-946). If no character was copied (for example only blanks, or an empty quoted string) it returns NULL, after updating slrflag (and setting altarg to NULL when slrflag was 1), leaving stringbase at the place where the scan stopped, which can be a blank rather than the terminating NUL (947-958).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the no-token path can leave stringbase at whitespace (e.g. `"" `), not the terminating NUL - right (943 stores sb, which stops at the blank at 886-889 after an empty quoted pair that sets no got_one). Slice cut the head; function read in full; INC_CHKCURSOR not read.

name: ftp_login
prose: Logs in to the FTP server (tnftp util.c:379-503; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure (rval, 476, 502). It copies luser and lpass, replaces them with "anonymous" and the anonpass option in anonymous mode, and calls ruserpass; a negative result sets code to -1 and goes to cleanup without printing a warning (389-410). While no user name is set it prompts for one with get_line; an input error prints "...; login aborted." and sets code to -1 (412-428); an empty answer uses the local name. In gate mode it appends "@host" to the user name (430-441). It sends USER; if the reply is CONTINUE it prompts for a password if none is set and sends PASS (443-454). If a reply is CONTINUE again it needs an account: an empty account prints "Login failed" and goes to cleanup, else it sends ACCT (455-470). A reply that is not COMPLETE, or a failed later ACCT, prints "Login failed" and goes to cleanup (471-475). Only a CONTINUE reply to USER or PASS is not a failure by itself. On success it sets rval to 1, stores the user name, and, unless proxy is set, sets connected to -1, gets the remote info, runs the "init" macro if one exists and updates the local and remote working directories (476-492). cleanup frees and zeroes the user, password and account strings and returns rval (494-502).
note: [R:right] reviewer: no warning on ruserpass failure/EOF; USER/PASS CONTINUE is not failure - right (407-410 sets code=-1 silently; 443-455 treat CONTINUE as a step toward PASS/ACCT). Slice cut the head; function read in full; ruserpass, command and getpass not read.

name: tzset_unlocked
prose: Re-reads the TZ environment (or the default zone) into the global local-time state unless it is already current; defined at localtime.c:1881-1947 (slice cut the head); it returns nothing. In a loop it picks the zone name: NULL when wall is true, otherwise getenv("TZ"), starts from the global lclptr, and, for a name that begins with the zoneinfo directory prefix, abbreviates it (1889-1911). If the zone data is still fresh (tz_change_interval and fresh_tzdata) and either a name is set and lcl_is_set is positive with the same stored name, or there is no name and lcl_is_set is negative, it returns without changes (1913-1917). With read-write locking it upgrades to the write lock and repeats the loop once, returning if the upgrade fails (1919-1923). It then (allocating the state if needed when ALL_STATE) calls zoneinit(sp, name, flags); on an error it loads the empty (UTC) zone and sets the abbreviation to "-00" unless name is NULL and the error was ENOENT (1930-1938). A name shorter than lcl_TZname is copied into it (1939-1943). It calls settzname and sets lcl_is_set to 1 if the name is shorter than the buffer, -1 if longer, and 0 if equal; with name NULL, namelen is the buffer size plus one, so lcl_is_set is -1 (1946, 1893). With wall true, name is NULL and zoneinit calls tzload with a NULL name, which is the default zone and not UTC; UTC is used only for an empty name or as the fallback after an error (1835-1858).
note: [R:right] reviewer: the lcl_is_set sign is reversed (a shorter name gives 1, not -1); wall=true loads TZDEFAULT, not UTC - right on the sign (1946) and on the NULL name path (zoneinit 1849-1850 passes NULL to tzload, whose NULL handling I did not read, so "default zone" is by the tz code's convention). Slice cut the head; function read in full, zoneinit read; tzload, settzname, fresh_tzdata and the lock helpers not read.

name: grow_nitems_alloc
prose: Grows an allocation count by about half and returns the byte size of the new allocation; defined at zic.c:644-659 (slice cut the head). It computes addend = (*nitems_alloc >> 1) + 1 (646). When ckd_add and ckd_mul are available it adds addend to *nitems_alloc in place (this write happens even if the check fails later) and multiplies the new count by itemsize into a local product; if neither overflowed and the product is at most INDEX_MAX it returns the product (649-651). Otherwise (no ckd macros) it requires the old count to be at most ((INDEX_MAX - 1) / 3 * 2) / itemsize, then increases *nitems_alloc by addend and returns the new count times itemsize (653-655); that bound keeps the product below about INDEX_MAX - 1 plus itemsize, so it cannot overflow ptrdiff_t for itemsize 2, and larger item sizes were not analysed. In both builds, when the checks fail it calls memory_exhausted("integer overflow") (658), which is not shown to return, so there is no value returned on that path.

Read in full; memory_exhausted not read (assumed not to return).

name: cachedb_handle_query
prose: Handles a query in unbound's cachedb module (cachedb.c:794-884; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and works through qstate. It clears is_cachedb_answer. If the module is not enabled, or the query is blacklisted, says no cache lookup, or a stub or forwarder forbids caching, it sets ext_state[id] to module_wait_module and returns (802-816). It then looks in unbound's internal cache; on a hit it sets module_finished and returns (820-834). Otherwise it looks in the external cache; on a hit it stores the answer into the internal cache (844). If serve_expired is configured and the entry is expired, it drops return_msg, sets module_wait_module, clears need_refetch and returns (850-858). If need_refetch is set and serve_expired_data has a timer it drops return_msg and sets module_wait_module and returns (859-864), so this wait applies only with the serve-expired timer. Otherwise it marks the answer as a cachedb answer and sets module_finished (866-870). With no external hit, if serve_expired_data, cachedb_check_when_serve_expired and no serve_expired_client_timeout apply it sends the expired answer with mesh_respond_serve_expired (873-879), and it sets module_wait_module (883).

name: cachedb_operate
prose: Event entry point of unbound's cachedb module (cachedb.c:921-968; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It reads the module environment and the per-query state iq. For a new or pass event with no iq it creates the state with cachedb_new, replying SERVFAIL through error_response and returning if that fails (932-939). With an iq, a new or pass event calls cachedb_handle_query and returns, and a moddone event calls cachedb_handle_response and returns (940-947). With an iq and an outbound entry (and none of the earlier events) it ignores the response and returns (948-954). An error event, whether or not an outbound entry or an iq exists, logs, replies SERVFAIL and returns (955-958); a moddone event with no iq sets ext_state[id] to module_finished and returns (960-963). Any other event logs "bad event for cachedb" and replies SERVFAIL (966-967).

Slice cut the head; function read in full; cachedb_new and cachedb_handle_response not read.

name: getentropy_fallback
prose: Fills buf with len bytes of pseudo-random data by hashing system state with SHA-512 (the real name is getentropy_fallback, getentropy_osx.c:204-417; the slice 255-417 is its tail). It saves errno and chooses the repeat count (a smaller one when the process id equals the one of the previous call, 229-237). For each chunk of up to 64 bytes it initialises a SHA512 context and, repeat times, hashes the time of day, several sysctl values, process and session ids, signal masks, addresses and the page contents of mapped memory, resource usage, file system information for "." and "/" and for descriptor 0 (stat results, and, when fstat on descriptor 0 yields -1 and the (unset) mode looks like a regular file, FIFO or socket, the statvfs, statfs and related calls on it), the child resource usage and the time of day again (HX and HD hash the values whether the call failed or not, 240-407). It finalises the digest and copies min(64, remaining) bytes into buf (409-411). After the loop it zeroes the context and the digest with explicit_bzero, restores errno and returns 0 (413-416); this is the only return in the function. Failing system calls are not treated as errors; their results are only hashed.
note: [R:right] reviewer: the fstat failure is not ignored; the code branches on e == -1 and uses st - right (365-369: the descriptor-0 file-type test runs when fstat returned -1, the reverse of what is intended, and then uses st). Fixed under the real name getentropy_fallback; read in part: head and tail (204-242, 363-417) and a scan of the HX calls in between (242-398), the middle was not read line by line.

name: remote_control_callback
prose: Event callback for one unbound remote-control connection (remote.c:4291-4347; slice cut the head); it returns 0 except where the handshake is still pending. For an event other than NETEVENT_NOERROR it logs a timeout when it was one, calls clean_point(rc, s) and returns 0 (4298-4303). For an SSL connection it performs SSL_do_handshake; any result other than 1 returns remote_handshake_later(rc, s, c, r, error), whose return value is passed on, so this covers both a handshake that must be retried and a failed handshake (4304-4311). After a successful handshake it clears shake_state. If certificates are not in use it logs an unauthenticated connection; if they are in use it requires the verification result X509_V_OK and a peer certificate, and otherwise cleans the connection up and returns 0 (4316-4337). Then it fills res with the SSL object and the descriptor, calls handle_req, logs completion, cleans the connection up and returns 0 (4340-4346).

name: dt_msg_queue_submit
prose: Queues a dnstap message buffer for the writer thread (dtstream.c:235-302; the packet name dt_msg_queue_push does not exist and the slice 255-509 starts inside this function); it returns nothing and takes ownership of buf. It returns without doing anything if buf is NULL (241). It frees buf and returns if len is 0 or mq is NULL (242-253), and frees buf and returns after logging an out-of-memory message if the entry allocation fails (256-261). Otherwise it locks the queue, decides whether to start a timer (list empty or the writer is not writing) and whether to wake the writer at once (message count equal to DTIO_MSG_FOR_WAKEUP, or the size crossing 90 percent of maxsize) (267-277). If the queued size plus len would exceed maxsize it unlocks, frees buf and the entry and returns, dropping the message (279-286). Otherwise it adds len to cursize, increments msgcount, appends the entry at the end of the list and unlocks (287-297); after unlocking it calls dt_msg_queue_start_timer when a wakeup or timer start was decided (299-301).
note: [R:n/a] still-rejected only for the wrong name ("function name not in the source slice"); fixed under the real name dt_msg_queue_submit. Read in full; the comment at 279-281 (drop reason) and dt_msg_queue_start_timer not read.

name: ipsecmod_handle_query
prose: Handles a query inside unbound's ipsecmod module (ipsecmod.c:386-464; slice cut the head); it returns nothing and works through qstate. If the module is not enabled or the query is not whitelisted it sets ext_state[id] to module_wait_module and returns (393-396). If the IPSECKEY lookup has not been done yet, it sets no_cache_store for an A or AAAA query, sets module_wait_module and returns (399-412). Otherwise, if an IPSECKEY rrset with data exists, it calls ipsecmod_error and returns if the data is bogus and bogus data is not ignored, and likewise returns after ipsecmod_error if the hook fails while ipsecmod_strict is set (415-433). It then finds the answer rrset of the return message and, if its TTL is above ipsecmod_max_ttl, sets the rrset TTL and all its RR TTLs to ipsecmod_max_ttl, and if the message TTL is also above the limit lowers it and recomputes (not clamps) prefetch_ttl with PREFETCH_TTL_CALC and serve_expired_ttl as the new ttl plus the configured serve_expired_ttl (436-453). It stores the reply in the cache (logging an error when that fails, which does not stop it) and sets ext_state[id] to module_finished (457-463).

name: response_type_from_server
prose: Classifies a DNS response from a name server (unbound iterator, iter_resptype.c:108-309; slice cut the head) and returns one of the RESPONSE_TYPE_ values. It returns THROWAWAY if msg or request is NULL or the TC flag is set (116-121). For NXDOMAIN it returns REC_LAME when RA is set, AA is not and rdset is 0, CNAME if the answer section has a CNAME for the query name, else ANSWER (124-139); any other non-NOERROR rcode returns THROWAWAY (143-144). For NOERROR it takes the origin zone from dp (default root) and scans the answer section: an NS rrset for a qtype of ANY or NS below the zone returns ANSWER with AA set or REFERRAL otherwise (167-176); an answer of the query type and name returns ANSWER with AA, else leaves the loop (183-193); CNAMEs followed to their target (195-200). After the loop it returns ANSWER for qtype ANY, and CNAME if a CNAME was followed (203-210). In the authority section, an SOA at or above the query name returns REC_LAME (RA set, AA not set, rdset 0) or ANSWER (215-227). An NS rrset in the authority section: equal to the origin zone returns REC_LAME (RA, no AA, rdset 0), else THROWAWAY (no answers, no AA, rdset 0), else ANSWER, so with rdset nonzero it returns ANSWER (242-259); an NS at or above the origin zone returns THROWAWAY if rdset else LAME (263-267); an NS below it returns REFERRAL (271-281). An entirely empty message returns THROWAWAY until empty_nodata_found reaches EMPTY_NODATA_RETRY_COUNT (when that pointer is given) and ANSWER after, or ANSWER at once without the pointer (294-303). Otherwise REC_LAME with RA set, AA not set and rdset 0, else ANSWER (306-308).
note: [R:right] reviewer: an NS rrset equal to the originating zone with rdset nonzero returns THROWAWAY/LAME, but the code returns ANSWER - right (245-259 each test !rdset). Slice cut the head; function read in full; get_cname_target and the dname helpers not read.

name: scrub_sanitize
prose: Removes resource record sets from a parsed DNS response that a name server for zonename should not be trusted for (unbound iter_scrub.c:974-1134; slice cut the head); it returns 1 at its only return (1133). The first rrset is allowed to stay if it is a DNAME in the answer section whose owner is a strict parent of the query name and a subdomain of the zone, even though its name differs from the query name (986-995). It then removes the following answer-section rrsets whose owner differs from the query name (997-1013). Second pass over all rrsets (1022-1132): an A or AAAA rrset is length-checked and removed if that fails (1027-1031); an A, AAAA, SVCB or HTTPS rrset is removed if priv_rrset_bad says it is bad (1035-1048); an rrset whose owner is not within the zone is removed (with its referencing additional section being flagged for removal), except that an NS rrset above the zone in a NOERROR/NODATA reply without SOA is kept for lame classification, and an out-of-zone A/AAAA is stored in the cache instead of being kept when harden_glue is off (1057-1087). NS rrsets in answer or authority sections record their owner (1088-1097); additional-section rrsets are removed when del_addi was flagged (1098-1102); overreaching NSEC rrsets are removed (1104-1109); with harden_unverified_glue, A/AAAA glue that is not below the NS owner is marked as unverified glue, cached and removed from the message (1110-1128); everything else stays.
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits that the first answer-section DNAME differing from qname is allowed to stay - right (989-995, before the answer-section loop). Slice cut the head; function read in full; scrub_sanitize_rr_length, priv_rrset_bad, store_rrset and sanitize_nsec_is_overreach not read.

name: handle_cname_response
prose: Collects the CNAME and DNAME chain of a response for the iterator (iterator.c:532-579; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It starts with *mname and *mname_len set to the chased query name (537-538). For each answer rrset it adds a DNAME that is a parent of the current name to the prepend-answer list unless it is already there, without following it (548-554). It adds a CNAME for the current name to the list unless the list already holds it, and in that case moves *mname to the CNAME's target (556-562); a CNAME that is already in the prepend list is neither added nor followed, so *mname is not advanced for it. An out-of-memory result from iter_add_prepend_answer returns 0 at once (551-552, 560-561). It then adds every NSEC and NSEC3 rrset from the authority section to the authority prepend list, returning 0 if that fails (568-577), and returns 1 (578).

Slice cut the head; function read in full; the iter_*prepend helpers and get_cname_target not read.

name: apply_ixfr
prose: Applies a received IXFR (a list of deletions and additions framed by SOA records) to the zone z (unbound authzone.c:4919-5052; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on any failure, including the "soft failure" case. It walks the resource records of the transfer chunks; a record that cannot be read returns 0 (4937-4943). The first record must be an SOA and so must the second, otherwise it returns 0 (4947-4954). An SOA whose rdata is shorter than 22 bytes returns 0 (4957). The first SOA records its serial and sets delmode to 1, and ixfr_start_serial must succeed (checked against xfr->serial) or the function returns 0 (4959-4969); a later SOA with the same serial counts up and returns 0 if it is the second record, and when it is the third occurrence it stores the serial in xfr->serial and leaves the loop (4970-4990). Each SOA that does not end the loop then toggles delmode (4997), so the first SOA ends up in add mode. In delete mode a record is removed with az_remove_rr_decompress (a failure returns 0; a record that did not exist sets softfail); in add mode a record is inserted with az_insert_rr_decompress unless it is the first record, which is skipped, so the first SOA is not added at that point (a failure returns 0; a duplicate sets softfail) (5005-5042). After the loop, if softfail is set it returns 0 so that the full zone is fetched, otherwise it returns 1 (5047-5051).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: claims the first SOA is skipped for addition, but the code toggles delmode so it is added - wrong: delmode is toggled to 0 by the first SOA (4962, 4997) but the add branch has `else if(rr_counter != 0)` (5022) so a record with rr_counter 0 (the first SOA) is skipped; the SOA with the transfer serial that is added is the later one. Slice cut the head; function read in full; the az_* helpers and ixfr_start_serial not read.

name: xfr_set_timeout
prose: Schedules the next probe timer of an authoritative-zone transfer task (unbound authzone.c:6994-7073; slice cut the head); it returns nothing. It starts next_probe at the current time, or at xfr->lease_time when that is set and failure is 0 (7004-7006). On success it resets the backoff to 0; on failure it sets it to 3 or doubles it, capped at AUTH_TRANSFER_MAX_BACKOFF (7008-7017). If the zone exists it adds the refresh interval (or retry after a failure), or the expiry if that is smaller, adds the backoff on failure, and, if lease_time plus expiry lies before the computed time but after now, uses that instead (7019-7033). If the zone does not exist it adds only the backoff to the starting time (7034-7037). It creates the timer if needed and returns after logging if that allocation fails, leaving no timer set (7039-7050). It records the worker and env, computes the delay (zero when the time has passed), and, when lookup_only is set and masters exist, uses a zero delay and sets only_lookup on the probe task if it has no worker (7052-7064). It then logs the delay and arms the timer with comm_timer_set (7065-7072).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits the no-zone branch: when !have_zone, next_probe is now+backoff only, not refresh/retry/expiry - right (7034-7037; with the lease_time start when not failure). Slice cut the head; function read in full; comm_timer helpers not read.

name: doq_conn_write_streams
prose: Writes pending DNS-over-QUIC stream data and QUIC packets of conn through ngtcp2 (unbound listen_dnsport.c:5337-5483; slice cut the head); it returns 1 normally and 0 when it closes the connection because of an error, and stores in *err_drop (if non-NULL) whether closing failed. It loops over the connection's write-stream list starting at stream_write_first, with a final pass with stream id -1 and no data when no stream is left (5340-5383). For each stream it sets the data vectors from the not-yet-written part of the length prefix and the answer, sets the FIN flag and the MORE flag when another stream follows (5355-5389), and calls ngtcp2_conn_writev_stream. A negative result: NGTCP2_ERR_WRITE_MORE adds the written bytes to nwrite, marks the stream done when fully written, moves to the next stream and continues the loop without returning (5397-5407); NGTCP2_ERR_STREAM_DATA_BLOCKED and NGTCP2_ERR_STREAM_SHUT_WR set an application error and close the connection (doq_conn_close_error), set *err_drop to 1 if that failed, and return 0 (5408-5437); any other error logs, sets a library error, closes the connection and returns 0 the same way (5440-5454). On a nonnegative result it adds the written data to the stream and marks it done when complete (5459-5463). A result of 0 disables further writing, updates the packet transmit time and returns 1 (5464-5468). Otherwise it sends the packet with doq_send_pkt, stops the loop if a packet was blocked or max_packets (65535) were sent, and moves to the next stream (5470-5479). After the loop it updates the packet transmit time and returns 1 (5481-5482).
note: [R:right] reviewer: omits NGTCP2_ERR_WRITE_MORE, which continues instead of returning 0 - right (5397-5407). Slice cut the head; function read in full; ngtcp2 and the doq_* helpers not read.

name: mesh_attach_sub
prose: Creates (or finds) a sub-query state of the mesh and attaches it to qstate's state (unbound mesh.c:1260-1282; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It calls mesh_add_sub and returns 0 if that fails (1267-1269). It notes whether the sub-state had no super states before (super_set.count == 0), calls mesh_state_attachment to link it below qstate's mesh state and returns 0 if that fails (1270-1272). If the sub-state has no reply list and no callback list, was detached before and now has exactly one super state, it decrements mesh->num_detached_states (1274-1278). It returns 1 (1281).

name: serviced_check_qname
prose: Compares the query name of a received packet with the query name stored in qbuf (unbound outside_network.c:3000-3046); it returns 1 if both name sequences match label for label, otherwise 0. It returns 0 at once if the packet limit is below 17 bytes (3006-3007). It walks the packet's name from offset 12 and qbuf's name from offset 10 in step. A compression pointer in the packet name is followed (after checking that the pointer's bytes and its target are inside the packet limit); more than MAX_COMPRESS_PTRS pointers return 0 (3012-3023). For a plain label it returns 0 if d2 is beyond qbuf+qbuflen, the two label lengths differ, the length exceeds LDNS_MAX_LABELLEN, the label would reach the packet limit, or the label bytes differ with memcmp (3025-3039); it then moves to the next labels. It returns 1 when both reach the end of the name (3011, 3045). The code checks d2 against qbuf+qbuflen only before a label, not that d2 plus the label length stays inside qbuf.

name: serviced_tcp_callback
prose: Callback for a TCP (or TLS) query to an upstream server in unbound (outside_network.c:3139-3235); it always returns 0 (3182, 3234), but its effects depend on the outcome. It clears sq->pending, logs an address on error, and on success marks that TCP works for the address in the infra cache (3153-3159). With dnstap and the right logging options it sends the response message to dnstap (3160-3174). If the status is serviced_query_TCP_EDNS and the response rcode is FORMERR or NOTIMPL, it sets the status to serviced_query_TCP_EDNS_fallback, starts the query again with serviced_tcp_initiate and returns 0 without calling the callbacks (3175-3182). If the status is the EDNS fallback and the rcode is NOERROR, NXDOMAIN or YXDOMAIN, it records "no EDNS" for the server in the infra cache unless DNSSEC is wanted (logging an error if that fails) and sets the status to serviced_query_TCP (3183-3199). For tcp_upstream or ssl_upstream queries it updates the round-trip time: a failure records -1, and a success with time moving forward records the measured time in milliseconds if it is below 60000 (3200-3224). It then ensures a reply structure (using a local one if rep is NULL), copies the server address into it and calls serviced_callbacks(sq, error, c, rep) (3226-3233) before returning 0.

name: outnet_serviced_query
prose: Finds or creates a serviced (deduplicated) outgoing query and registers a callback on it (unbound outside_network.c:3474-3597; slice cut the head); it returns the serviced_query or NULL. It obtains a region from the allocator, returning NULL if that fails (3495-3496); if qstate has an outgoing EDNS option list it copies it into that region and uses the copy while the query callbacks run, returning NULL after releasing the region if the copy fails (3497-3505). If inplace_cb_query_call fails it releases the region and returns NULL without having put the original edns_opts_back_out list back, since the restore comes only after that call (3507-3515). It then restores the original list, appends a configured client-string option if the address matches, generates the query packet in buff and looks up an existing serviced query (3517-3528). If none exists it optionally increments the rate limit counter and returns NULL with *was_ratelimited set when the rate limit applies, except for random pass-through (3531-3551); it then creates the serviced query, undoing the rate-limit count and returning NULL on failure, and allocates the callback entry in its region, undoing the rate-limit count, deleting the new query from the tree and returning NULL if that fails (3554-3577). If one exists, it releases the region and allocates a callback entry, returning NULL on failure (3580-3589). It fills the callback entry, links it at the head of sq->cblist and returns sq (3592-3596).

name: outnet_tcp_take_into_use
prose: Takes a free pending TCP entry from the outside network and uses it for the waiting query w (unbound outside_network.c:661-832; slice cut the head); it returns 1 on success and 0 on failure. It clears two toggle flags of the comm point (670-671), returns 0 if SSL upstream is wanted but no SSL context exists (676-679), opens a TCP socket with outnet_get_tcp_fd (returns 0 on -1) and binds it to the pending entry with pick_outgoing_tcp (returns 0 on failure) (682-689), sets it non-blocking and starts connecting (a connect error other than EINPROGRESS logs if the error warrants it, closes the socket and returns 0; with fast open the plain connect is skipped for non-SSL TCP, 691-751). For TLS it creates the SSL object (on failure closes the comm point and returns 0), sets the shake state, copies the authentication name (an allocation failure frees the SSL object, closes the comm point and returns 0) and sets the name on the SSL object (a failure frees everything and returns 0) (752-791). Then it links the pending entry to w, increments num_tcp_outgoing, removes the entry from the free list, fills the reuse and comm point fields and copies the address, removing an existing tree entry first if the key is set (792-811). It records the SSL state and authentication name in the reuse structure, frees any old name, inserts the reuse entry in the tree, calls outnet_tcp_take_query_setup(s, pend, w) and returns 1 (813-831). The write timer on w is set inside outnet_tcp_take_query_setup with comm_timer_set(w->timer, &tv) built from w->timeout (outside_network.c:650-656) and not in this function.

Slice cut the head; function read in full, conditional-compilation variants (OSX fast open, MSG_FASTOPEN, Winsock) summarised together.

name: sldns_fget_token_l
prose: Reads one token from file f into token (unbound sldns parse.c:33-224; slice cut the head); it returns the token length, -1 or 0. delim defaults to LDNS_PARSE_NORMAL. It reads characters with getc, treats '\r' as a blank, tracks parentheses (a depth counter p, outside quotes and comments) and ';' comments, and a leading '"' in delim starts in quoted mode (44-60). If a ')' makes the depth negative it terminates the token and returns 0 as soon as the next character is read, without that character being counted for line_nr (82-86). Newlines inside parentheses or comments are turned into blanks and counted in *line_nr when line_nr is non-NULL (98-147), and a newline seen elsewhere increments *line_nr as it is processed (156-157, 186-189). If the token limit would be reached (limit > 0) it terminates the buffer and returns -1 (140-143, 179-182). A delimiter at depth 0 after at least one character ends the token (jump to tokenread) unless only blanks have been seen, in which case the token is restarted (155-169). At EOF it returns the number of characters read (199-201). If the loop ended with nothing read or with unbalanced parentheses it returns -1 (203-209). At tokenread it skips the following delimiter characters with sldns_fskipcs_l and returns -1 if the parentheses are unbalanced, else the token length (212-223).

name: sldns_bget_keyword_data
prose: Reads a keyword token and then a data token from the sldns buffer b (unbound sldns parse.c:491-522; the excerpt in the packet is its tail, so the real name is sldns_bget_keyword_data). It returns -1 if strlen(keyword) is at least LDNS_MAX_KEYWORDLEN or the keyword buffer cannot be allocated (499-503). It reads the first token into that buffer with delimiter k_del and limit data_limit; if the result is 0 or -1 it frees the buffer and returns -1 (505-509). If the token starts with keyword (a strncmp over strlen(keyword) characters, so a longer token that begins with the keyword also matches) it frees the buffer and returns the result of sldns_bget_token(b, data, d_del, 0) for the data token, with no length limit (512-517); otherwise it frees the buffer and returns -1 (518-520).

name: sldns_buffer_skip
prose: Advances the position of buffer by count bytes (sbuffer.h:258-262; slice cut the head). It asserts that buffer->_position + count <= buffer->_limit (260), where count is converted to an unsigned type, so a negative count that would move the position before the start makes the sum wrap to a huge value and the assert fails, while a negative count within the current position passes it; then it adds count to _position (261). With NDEBUG the assertion is compiled out and no check remains. It returns nothing.
note: [R:right] reviewer: the assert catches a negative count before the start via the unsigned wrap; the earlier prose said unchecked and its postcondition on wraparound contradicted its precondition - right (260). Slice cut the head; function read in full.

name: config_set_option
prose: Sets one unbound configuration option from the text pair (opt, val) (config_file.c:541-950; slice cut the head); it returns 1 when the option was recognised and applied and 0 when it was not or the value was rejected. It returns 0 for a NULL opt (545) and appends a ':' to opt when it has none and a copy fits in a 64-byte buffer (546-549). It then walks one long if/else chain comparing opt with the option names; most entries are macros that parse val (yes/no, a number that must be non-zero or may be zero, a string that replaces and frees the old one, a list that is replaced, appended to or inserted uniquely). Special cases include: num-threads always returns 0 (557-559); outgoing-port-permit and outgoing-port-avoid, local-zone and val-override-date return the result of cfg_mark_ports, cfg_parse_local_zone or a time conversion (560-575); tls-protocols returns 0 for an invalid value (638-641); local-data-ptr calls cfg_ptr_reverse on the option name argument opt and returns the result of cfg_strlist_insert (578-580); an unrecognised name reaches the final else and returns 0, and a successful branch falls to return 1 (947-949). Because most options are table macros, the exact fields updated are those named in the macros (for example the global mirrors of max-ttl, serve-expired and the RTT limits are updated where the option sets them).
note: [R:wrong] reviewer: the local-data-ptr claim is wrong; cfg_ptr_reverse is called on val/the inserted string, not opt, and the return is not just cfg_strlist_insert - wrong on the argument: line 579 is `cfg_ptr_reverse((char*)opt)` and 580 returns cfg_strlist_insert(&cfg->local_data, ptr) directly (so the reviewer's claim about opt is mistaken, although the old claim that the "ptr" option name is used as the argument is odd). Partly read: head (541-575), local-data-ptr (578-580), tail (930-950) and a grep of the rest; the macro-driven option table (550-932) was scanned, not read line by line, so field mirrors such as MAX_TTL are only noted generally.
